Fetch a page

Fetching returns the decoded body of one URL. The call follows redirects, reports the final URL, and refuses addresses that resolve to the local machine or to a private range, because a page can contain a link that points anywhere. See Limits for the byte and time budgets that apply to every request.

Parameters

The only required parameter is the URL itself. The scheme must be http or https; every other scheme is rejected before any socket is opened. The result carries the content type, the character set that was used to decode the body, and the number of characters that survived extraction, so a caller can tell a real article from a page whose body is rendered later.

result = fetch("https://example.com/guide")
print(result.text)

When the body is not text, the call returns a short explanation instead of the bytes. That keeps binary payloads out of the model's context.
